meta.title: Seas & Oceans
meta.subtitle: Oceans, seas, gulfs, bays and straits

items.name: Pacific Ocean
items.blurb: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's five oceanic divisions.

items.name: Atlantic Ocean
items.blurb: The Atlantic Ocean is the second largest of the world's five oceans, with an area of about 85,133,000 square kilometers. It covers approximately 17% of Earth's surface and about 24% of its water surface area.

items.name: Indian Ocean
items.blurb: The Indian Ocean is the third-largest of the world's five oceanic divisions, covering 70,560,000 km2 or approximately 20% of the water area of Earth's surface. It is bounded by Asia to the north, Africa to the west and Australia to the east.

items.name: Arctic Ocean
items.blurb: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest of the world's five oceanic divisions. It spans an area of approximately 14,060,000 km2 and is the coldest of the world's oceans.

items.name: Southern Ocean
items.blurb: The Southern Ocean, also known as the Antarctic Ocean, comprises the southernmost waters of the World Ocean, generally taken to be south of 60° S latitude and encircling Antarctica.

items.name: Mediterranean Sea
facts: Spain, France, Italy, Monaco, Slovenia, Croatia, Montenegro, Albania +14 more
items.blurb: The Mediterranean Sea is an intercontinental sea situated between Europe, Asia, and Africa.

items.name: Caribbean Sea
facts: Mexico, Belize, Cuba, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama +12 more
items.blurb: The Caribbean Sea is a sea of the North Atlantic Ocean in the tropics of the Western Hemisphere, located south of the Gulf of Mexico and southwest of the Sargasso Sea.

items.name: South China Sea
facts: Vietnam, Taiwan, Malaysia, Cambodia, China, Philippines, Brunei, Indonesia
items.blurb: The South China Sea is a marginal sea of the Western Pacific Ocean.

items.name: Arabian Sea
items.blurb: The Arabian Sea is a region of sea in the northern Indian Ocean, bounded on the west by the Arabian Peninsula, Gulf of Aden and Guardafui Channel, on the northwest by Gulf of Oman and Iran, on the north by Pakistan, on the east by India, and on the southeast by the Laccadive Sea and the Maldives, and on the southwest by Somalia.

items.name: Black Sea
facts: Bulgaria, Russia, Ukraine, Romania, Türkiye, Georgia
items.blurb: The Black Sea is a marginal sea located between Europe and Asia, east of the Balkans, south of the East European Plain, west of the Caucasus, and north of Anatolia. It is bordered by Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania, Russia, Turkey, and Ukraine.

items.name: Caspian Sea
items.blurb: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland body of water, also described as the world's largest lake and usually referred to as a full-fledged sea.

items.name: Red Sea
facts: Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Djibouti, Eritrea, Yemen, Israel, Jordan
items.blurb: The Red Sea is a mediterranean sea lying between the Arabian Peninsula and Africa. It is an inlet of the Indian Ocean.

items.name: Baltic Sea
facts: Sweden, Finland, Russia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Germany +1 more
items.blurb: The Baltic Sea is an arm of the Atlantic Ocean that is enclosed by the countries of Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Russia, and Sweden. Geophysically, it is surrounded by the Scandinavian Peninsula and the North and Central European Plain regions.

items.name: North Sea
facts: Norway, Denmark, Germany, Netherlands, Belgium, France, United Kingdom
items.blurb: The North Sea lies between Great Britain, Denmark, Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, and France. A sea on the European continental shelf, it connects to the Atlantic Ocean through the English Channel in the south and the Norwegian Sea in the north.

items.name: Bering Sea
items.blurb: The Bering Sea is a marginal sea of the Northern Pacific Ocean. It forms, along with the Bering Strait, the divide between the two largest landmasses on Earth: Eurasia and the Americas.

items.name: Sea of Japan
facts: Russia, Japan, North Korea, South Korea
items.blurb: The Sea of Japan is the marginal sea between the Japanese archipelago, Sakhalin, the Korean Peninsula, and the mainland of the Russian Far East. The Japanese archipelago separates the sea from the Pacific Ocean.

items.name: Sea of Okhotsk
items.blurb: The Sea of Okhotsk is a marginal sea of the northwestern Pacific Ocean.

items.name: Philippine Sea
facts: Micronesia, United States, Indonesia, Japan, Palau, Philippines, Taiwan
items.blurb: The Philippine Sea is a marginal sea of the Western Pacific Ocean east of the Philippine Archipelago and the largest sea in the world, occupying an estimated surface area of 5 million square kilometers. The Philippine Sea Plate forms the floor of the sea.

items.name: Tasman Sea
items.blurb: The Tasman Sea is a marginal sea of the South Pacific Ocean, situated between Australia and New Zealand. It measures about 2,000 km across and about 2,800 km from north to south.

items.name: Coral Sea
facts: Australia, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, France
items.blurb: The Coral Sea is a marginal sea of the South Pacific off the northeast coast of Australia, and classified as an interim Australian bioregion. The Coral Sea extends 2,000 kilometres down the Australian north-east coast to latitude 30° south.

items.name: Barents Sea
items.blurb: The Barents Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean, located off the northern coasts of Norway and Russia and divided between Norwegian and Russian territorial waters.

items.name: Norwegian Sea
items.blurb: The Norwegian Sea is a marginal sea, grouped with either the Atlantic Ocean or the Arctic Ocean, northwest of Norway between the North Sea and the Greenland Sea, adjoining the Barents Sea to the northeast.

items.name: Greenland Sea
items.blurb: The Greenland Sea is a body of water that borders Greenland to the west, the Svalbard archipelago to the east, Fram Strait and the Arctic Ocean to the north, and the Norwegian Sea and Iceland to the south.

items.name: Labrador Sea
items.blurb: The Labrador Sea is an arm of the North Atlantic Ocean between the Labrador Peninsula and Greenland. The sea is flanked by continental shelves to the southwest, northwest, and northeast.

items.name: Beaufort Sea
items.blurb: The Beaufort Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean, located north of the Northwest Territories, Yukon, and Alaska, and west of the Canadian Arctic Archipelago. The sea is named after Sir Francis Beaufort, a hydrographer.

items.name: Yellow Sea
items.blurb: The Yellow Sea, also known as the North Sea, is a marginal sea of the Western Pacific Ocean located between mainland China and the Korean Peninsula, and can be considered the northwestern part of the East China Sea.

items.name: East China Sea
items.blurb: The East China Sea is a marginal sea of the Western Pacific Ocean, located directly offshore from East China.

items.name: Andaman Sea
items.blurb: The Andaman Sea is a marginal sea of the northeastern Indian Ocean bounded by the coastlines of Myanmar and Thailand along the Gulf of Martaban and the west side of the Malay Peninsula, and separated from the Bay of Bengal to its west by the Andaman Islands and the Nicobar Islands.

items.name: Java Sea
items.blurb: The Java Sea is an extensive shallow sea in Indonesia. It lies on the Sunda Shelf, between the islands of Borneo to the north, Java to the south, Sumatra to the west, and Sulawesi to the east.

items.name: Celebes Sea
items.blurb: The Celebes Sea or Sulawesi Sea of the western Pacific Ocean is bordered on the north by the Sulu Archipelago and Sulu Sea and Mindanao Island of the Philippines, on the east by the Sangihe Islands chain, on the south by Sulawesi's Minahasa Peninsula, and the west by northern Kalimantan in Indonesia.

items.name: Aegean Sea
items.blurb: The Aegean Sea is an elongated embayment of the Mediterranean Sea between Europe and Asia.

items.name: Adriatic Sea
facts: Italy, Slovenia, Croatia, Montenegro, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina
items.blurb: The Adriatic Sea is a body of water separating the Italian Peninsula from the Balkan Peninsula. The Adriatic is the northernmost arm of the Mediterranean Sea, extending from the Strait of Otranto to the northwest and the Po Valley.

items.name: Tyrrhenian Sea
items.blurb: The Tyrrhenian Sea is part of the Mediterranean Sea off the western coast of Italy. Its namesake is from the Tyrrhenian people, identified with the Etruscans of Italy.

items.name: Ionian Sea
items.blurb: The Ionian Sea is an elongated bay of the Mediterranean Sea.

items.name: Irish Sea
items.blurb: The Irish Sea is a 46,007 km2 body of water that separates the islands of Ireland, Isle of Man and Great Britain. It is linked to the Celtic Sea in the south by St George's Channel and to the Inner Seas off the West Coast of Scotland in the north by the North Channel.

items.name: Sargasso Sea
items.blurb: The Sargasso Sea is a region of the Atlantic Ocean bounded by four currents forming an ocean gyre. It is the only named sea without land boundaries.

items.name: Weddell Sea
items.blurb: The Weddell Sea is part of the Southern Ocean and contains the Weddell Gyre. Its land boundaries are defined by the bay formed from the coasts of Coats Land and the Antarctic Peninsula.

items.name: Ross Sea
items.blurb: The Ross Sea is a deep bay of the Southern Ocean in Antarctica, between Victoria Land and Marie Byrd Land and within the Ross Embayment, and is the southernmost sea on Earth.

items.name: Kara Sea
items.blurb: The Kara Sea is a marginal sea, separated from the Barents Sea to the west by the Kara Strait and Novaya Zemlya, and from the Laptev Sea to the east by the Severnaya Zemlya archipelago.

items.name: Laptev Sea
items.blurb: The Laptev Sea is a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean. It is located between the northern coast of Siberia, the Taimyr Peninsula, Severnaya Zemlya, and the New Siberian Islands.

items.name: White Sea
items.blurb: The White Sea is a southern inlet of the Barents Sea located on the northwest coast of Russia. It is surrounded by Karelia to the west, the Kola Peninsula to the north, and the Kanin Peninsula to the northeast.

items.name: Sea of Azov
items.blurb: The Sea of Azov is an inland shelf sea in Eastern Europe connected to the Black Sea by the narrow Strait of Kerch, and sometimes regarded as a northern extension of the Black Sea. The sea is bounded by Russia on the east, and by Ukraine on the northwest and southwest.

items.name: Sea of Marmara
items.blurb: The Sea of Marmara, also known as the Sea of Marmora, the Marmara Sea, or Propontis, is a small inland sea entirely within the borders of Turkey. It links the Black Sea and the Aegean Sea via the Bosporus and Dardanelles straits, separating Turkey's European and Asian sides.

items.name: Arafura Sea
items.blurb: The Arafura Sea, also known as the Arafuru Sea, lies to the southeast of the Malay Archipelago in the western Pacific Ocean, overlying the continental shelf between Australia and Western New Guinea, which is the Indonesian part of the Island of New Guinea.

items.name: Timor Sea
items.blurb: The Timor Sea is a relatively shallow sea in the Indian Ocean bounded to the north by the island of Timor with Timor-Leste to the north, Indonesia to the northwest, Arafura Sea to the east, and to the south by Australia.

items.name: Bohai Sea
items.blurb: The Bohai Sea is a gulf/inland sea approximately 77,000 km2 in area on the east coast of Mainland China. It is the northwestern and innermost extension of the Yellow Sea, to which it connects via the Bohai Strait.

items.name: Gulf of Mexico
items.blurb: The Gulf of Mexico is an oceanic basin and a marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean, mostly surrounded by the North American continent.

items.name: Persian Gulf
facts: Saudi Arabia, Iran, Oman, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Iraq
items.blurb: The Persian Gulf, sometimes called the Arabian Gulf, is a mediterranean sea in West Asia. The body of water is an extension of the Arabian Sea and the larger Indian Ocean located between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran.

items.name: Gulf of Guinea
facts: Liberia, Ivory Coast, Ghana, Togo, Benin, Nigeria, Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea +2 more
items.blurb: The Gulf of Guinea is the northeasternmost part of the tropical Atlantic Ocean from Cape Lopez in Gabon, north and west to Cape Palmas in Liberia. Null Island, defined as the intersection of the Equator and Prime Meridian, is in the gulf.

items.name: Gulf of Thailand
items.blurb: The Gulf of Thailand, historically known as the Gulf of Siam, is a shallow inlet adjacent to the southwestern South China Sea, bounded between the southwestern shores of Mainland Southeast Asia and the northern half of the Malay Peninsula.

items.name: Gulf of Aden
items.blurb: The Gulf of Aden is a deepwater gulf of the Indian Ocean between Yemen to the north, the Arabian Sea to the east, Djibouti to the west, and the Guardafui Channel, the Socotra Archipelago, Puntland in Somalia and Somaliland to the south.

items.name: Gulf of Oman
facts: United Arab Emirates, Oman, Pakistan, Iran
items.blurb: The Gulf of Oman or Sea of Oman, also known as Gulf of Makran or Sea of Makran, is a gulf in the Indian Ocean that connects the Arabian Sea with the Strait of Hormuz, which then runs to the Persian Gulf.

items.name: Gulf of Alaska
items.blurb: The Gulf of Alaska is an arm of the Pacific Ocean defined by the curve of the southern coast of Alaska, stretching from Kabuch Point in the Alaska Peninsula and Kodiak Island in the west to the Cape Spencer in the east, where Glacier Bay is found and start the Inside Passage.

items.name: Gulf of California
items.blurb: The Gulf of California, also known as the Sea of Cortés or Sea of Cortez, or less commonly as the Vermilion Sea, is a marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean that separates the Baja California peninsula from the Mexican mainland.

items.name: Gulf of Bothnia
items.blurb: The Gulf of Bothnia is an arm of the Baltic Sea lying between Sweden and Finland. It is divided into the Bothnian Sea and the more northerly Bothnian Bay, the two being separated by the Kvarken strait.

items.name: Gulf of Finland
items.blurb: The Gulf of Finland is the easternmost arm of the Baltic Sea. It extends between Finland to the north and Estonia to the south, to Saint Petersburg—the second largest city of Russia—to the east, where the river Neva drains into it.

items.name: Gulf of Carpentaria
items.blurb: The Gulf of Carpentaria is a sea off the northern coast of Australia. It is enclosed on three sides by northern Australia and bounded on the north by the eastern Arafura Sea, which separates Australia and New Guinea.

items.name: Great Australian Bight
items.blurb: The Great Australian Bight is a large oceanic bight off the central and western portions of the southern coastline of mainland Australia.

items.name: Gulf of St. Lawrence
items.blurb: The Gulf of St. Lawrence connects the Great Lakes to the Atlantic Ocean via the St. Lawrence River.

items.name: Gulf of Tonkin
items.blurb: The Gulf of Tonkin is a gulf at the northwestern portion of the South China Sea, located off the coasts of Tonkin and South China.

items.name: Gulf of Aqaba
items.blurb: The Gulf of Aqaba or Gulf of Eilat is a large gulf at the northern tip of the Red Sea, southeast of the Sinai Peninsula, and west of the Arabian Peninsula. Its coastline is divided among four countries: Egypt, Israel, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia.

items.name: Río de la Plata
items.blurb: The Río de la Plata, also called the River Plate or La Plata River in English, is the estuary formed by the confluence of the Uruguay River and the Paraná River at Punta Gorda.

items.name: Bay of Bengal
items.blurb: The Bay of Bengal forms the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, located between the Indian subcontinent and the Indochinese peninsula, south of the Bengal region. Spread across an area of 2,600,000 km2, it is bordered by many of the countries in South Asia and Southeast Asia.

items.name: Hudson Bay
items.blurb: Hudson Bay, sometimes called Hudson's Bay, is a large body of saltwater in northeastern Canada with a surface area of 1,230,000 km2. It is located north of Ontario, west of Quebec, northeast of Manitoba, and southeast of Nunavut, but politically entirely part of Nunavut.

items.name: Baffin Bay
items.blurb: Baffin Bay, located between Baffin Island and the west coast of Greenland, is defined by the International Hydrographic Organization as a marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean. It is sometimes considered a sea of the North Atlantic Ocean.

items.name: Bay of Biscay
items.blurb: The Bay of Biscay, also known as the Gulf of Biscay or the Gulf of Gascony, is a gulf of the northeast Atlantic Ocean located south of the Celtic Sea.

items.name: Chesapeake Bay
items.blurb: The Chesapeake Bay is the largest estuary in the United States.

items.name: Bay of Fundy
items.blurb: The Bay of Fundy is a bay between the Canadian provinces of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia, with a small portion touching the U.S. state of Maine. It is an arm of the Gulf of Maine and part of the Atlantic Ocean.

items.name: Strait of Gibraltar
items.blurb: The Strait of Gibraltar, also known as the Straits of Gibraltar, is a narrow strait that connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea and separates Europe from Africa. The two continents are separated by 7.7 nautical miles at its narrowest point.

items.name: Strait of Malacca
items.blurb: The Strait of Malacca is a narrow stretch of water, 900 kilometres long and from 65 to 250 km wide, between the Malay Peninsula to the northeast and the Indonesian island of Sumatra to the southwest, connecting the Andaman Sea and the South China Sea.

items.name: Bosporus
items.blurb: The Bosporus or Bosphorus Strait is a natural strait and an internationally significant waterway located in Turkey and straddled by the city of Istanbul.

items.name: Dardanelles
items.blurb: The Dardanelles, also known as the Strait of Gallipoli, is a narrow, natural strait and internationally significant waterway in northwestern Turkey that forms part of the continental boundary between Asia and Europe and separates Asian Turkey from European Turkey.

items.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
items.blurb: The Bab al-Mandab Strait, also written simply as the Bab al-Mandab or Bab el-Mandeb, is a strait and global chokepoint between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula and Djibouti and Eritrea in the Horn of Africa, connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.

items.name: Taiwan Strait
items.blurb: The Taiwan Strait is a 180-kilometer-wide strait separating the island of Taiwan and mainland Asia. The strait connects the South China Sea to the south, and the East China Sea to the north.

items.name: Bass Strait
items.blurb: Bass Strait is a strait separating the island state of Tasmania from the Australian mainland. The strait provides the most direct waterway between the Great Australian Bight and the Tasman Sea, and is also the only maritime route into the economically prominent Port Phillip Bay.

items.name: Torres Strait
items.blurb: The Torres Strait, also known as Zenadh Kes, is a strait between Australia and the Melanesian island of New Guinea. It is 150 km wide at its narrowest extent.

items.name: Korea Strait
items.blurb: The Korea Strait is a sea passage in East Asia between the Korean Peninsula and Japan. It connects the East China Sea, the Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan in the northwest Pacific Ocean.

items.name: Strait of Magellan
items.blurb: The Strait of Magellan, also called the Straits of Magellan, is a navigable sea route in southern Chile separating mainland South America to the north and the Tierra del Fuego archipelago to the south.

items.name: Davis Strait
items.blurb: Davis Strait is a southern arm of the Arctic Ocean that lies north of the Labrador Sea. It lies between mid-western Greenland and Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada.

items.name: Denmark Strait
items.blurb: The Denmark Strait is the strait that separates Greenland from Iceland.

items.name: English Channel
items.blurb: The English Channel, also known as the Channel, is an arm of the Atlantic Ocean that separates Southern England from northern France. It links to the southern part of the North Sea by the Strait of Dover at its northeastern end.

items.name: Mozambique Channel
items.blurb: The Mozambique Channel is an arm of the Indian Ocean located between the Southeast African countries of Madagascar and Mozambique.

items.name: Drake Passage
items.blurb: The Drake Passage or Sea of Hoces is the body of water between Cape Horn in Chile at the southern extreme of the South American mainland and the South Shetland Islands of Antarctica.

items.name: Skagerrak
items.blurb: The Skagerrak is a strait running between the North Jutlandic Island of Denmark, the east coast of Norway and the west coast of Sweden, connecting the North Sea and the Kattegat sea.
